goal: Hook: one invented worker's plan at 14, 16 and 25, and what changed it; the full plan template and the six models (plan, job card, cluster map, decision steps card, data table, portfolio) met again or for the first time
note: Family note goes home (English and Spanish): what the year explores, what may come home, and one work question to ask a family member or any trusted adult, or to answer for an invented worker or from a public profile; sharing is the student's choice; a student 18 or over gets the note and makes their own choices. A grade 8 plan may be brought, never required. Last ten minutes: unit 1 readiness check (ten minutes): the two items of APPROACH unit field 4 (a percent of a total and a dated pay figure) and two more, about two minutes each: the plan's parts and goals (g8-cd1-2-first-plan, g8-cd1-3-goals) and a job placed on the cluster map (g8-cd3-4-cluster-map), all last used in Exploration grade 8. The other assumed grade 8 rows are taught again in context, not sampled: g8-cd1-3r-revisit-goals on day 2, g8-cd2-5-values on day 3, g8-all2-2-learner-identity on day 4, g8-all1-3-study-habits and g8-all1-5-school-plan on day 5, g8-cd2-2-decision-steps on day 8. Its ten-minute reteach, a model of the same reading, opens day 2. Paper path: printed template; one dated job profile on the shared screen.

goal: The plan reopened or begun: near and far goals written with a date, the steps already taken toward each, and the date each is checked again
note: Opens with the ten-minute reteach for the students day 1's check flagged. Goals are private on the plan page, read only by the teacher. The near and far goals are written on SEL's goal steps card in its 9 to 12 form, the designed plan (the goal, dated steps, the trade-off accepted, a check date, a verdict; SEL STANDARD section 7, Shared steps), career adding the near and far pair and the dated check against the program of study. SEL 9 to 12's grade 9 year, the year before, grew the card into that plan page (g9-sm-plan-and-tidy, g9-sm-set-goal), so it is retrieval for a student who took it and taught from the card for one who did not; SEL g10-sm-set-goal (unit 11) comes later this year. No task asks about family income or work.

goal: Values in a career choice: name one's own values privately, weigh two against each other on an invented choice, and judge how they steer a choice of one's own
note: Private on the plan page; the class discusses only the invented choice. Short value cards, no scored inventory.

goal: Two learning moments traced on a timeline (one in school, one outside) and what each says about the student as a learner
note: Private on the plan page; a student may trace an invented learner's moments instead. Nothing about family circumstances is asked.

goal: A week's study log begun; what last year's school plan achieved, and the high school course plan revised with a reason
note: A student new to the course reviews last year's courses instead of a grade 8 plan. SEL g10-sm-stay-on-task comes later in SEL 9 to 12, so the log is a career task here. The log runs for a week and is rated on day 10.

goal: Twenty jobs sorted three ways on the cluster map: by cluster, by training level and by work setting
note: Curio Class writes the twenty sort cards, disabled workers among the workers shown. Each card has a dated pay figure with its source and year.

goal: Which of the three groupings helps the plan most, judged with a reason and written as a plan line
note: The first plan line of school results is drafted here (checked in unit 4, g10-all1-school-results).

goal: Field task, day 1: the class argues for its two shared clusters with the decision steps and a weighted criteria table, then tallies the ballot on the data table
note: A school that adds a lab, an employer or a program for a cluster may put it on the ballot first, never in place of the vote. The ballot is the class's; no student is steered. The decision steps card is SEL's stop-think-choose grown for career choices (SEL STANDARD section 7). SEL 9 to 12's grade 9 year, the year before, ran the six-step stop-think-choose (g9-rds-careful-thinking), so its steps are retrieval for a student who took it and taught from the card for one who did not; SEL g10-rds-careful-thinking comes later this year. The weighted criteria table, the second decision method, is taught here.

goal: Field task, day 2: each student chooses their own cluster from the other twelve with both decision methods and judges which method suits them; the piece and the plan's changed line are drafted; the study log, kept since day 5, rated in a first draft
note: A student whose first choice is a shared cluster takes their own from the other twelve. The plan is scored on its reasoning, never on the cluster chosen. Before the collect: the study log rated in draft and one habit named to strengthen (ALL1.R3), returned with written feedback on day 10. Last five minutes: collect the piece, the job card and the plan page.

goal: Plan day: written feedback on the field task piece and the plan lines returned; one piece revised; the study log rating revised from its feedback and one habit chosen to strengthen; the portfolio begun or reopened with the unit's best piece
note: Feedback on two or three look-fors, written after class on days 8 and 9, the study log rating among them (drafted day 9, revised here).

goal: End-of-unit assessment: the revised piece and plan lines scored on the rubric, with two unseen data items
